Commentary.Commentary: We are all set! The Umpires and the Players walk out to take the field to start the run chase. Pippa Kelly and Emma Walsingham are the opening batters for Scotland Women Under-19 with a mammoth target of 209 runs ahead of them. Shabnam has the new ball in hand for India Women Under-19 and is ready on the mark to start the attack. Let's play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Trisha Gongadi, the player of the moment is up for a chat after mounting a superb century. She says she is really proud and happy with the way she batted. Tells that her father is there to cheer for her as well. Mentions she knew she was going to open the batting and focused more on striking the ball after getting settled in. Is all delighted and says she didn't know about the record that she has achieved.

Scotland Women Under-19 were below average in the field and even when the bowlers were bowling good deliveries, the efforts in the field gave away easy runs to the batters. They were nowhere close to bringing up any pressure on the scoring and India was clearly a stronger team with the bat. Scotland Women Under-19 now have a target of 209 runs which is never been chased down in U19 Women's cricket. Will there be a miracle happening or will India Women Under-19 take home another easy win? Let's find out in the run chase.

India Women Under-19 brought up the biggest total of the tournament setting up a formidable first innings score of 208 with the loss of just one wicket in the name of Kamalini G. Brilliant innings from the inform Trisha Gongadi who brought up her first hundred of the tournament, playing an unbeaten inning of 110 off just 59 deliveries. Kamalini G, her opening partner also crossed her first FIFTY run mark, putting up a first-wicket partnership of 147 runs, the highest in Women's U-19 T20 Internationals. India Women Under-19 were asked to bat first by Scotland and the Indian batters came firing on all cylinders. The run rate never dropped under 10 runs an over throughout the innings, thanks to the brilliance of Trisha Gongadi, Kamalini G, and Sanika Chalke who finished well too for her 29 off 20 deliveries, taking the team to 208 runs in 20 overs.
Full and straight outside the off-stump line, Sanika Chalke shuffles across to play the lap shot but misses. India Women Under-19 finish with a mammoth score of 208/1.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities and it is now time for the action to kick off at the Bayuemas Oval, Kuala Lumpur. It is still very overcast as the umpires and players walk out to the middle. The players of Scotland Women Under-19 take their respective fielding positions. Out walk the Indian opening pair of Kamalini G and Trisha Gongadi. Gabriella Fontenla has the new ball and will begin the proceedings for Scotland. Off we go...

We are just a few minutes away from the start! But before that, the two sets of players walk out to the middle with the match officials for the anthems. It will be Scotland's first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Stacy-Ann King is pitchside. She begins by informing about the dimensions and says it is 68 meters straight and 58 meters on the squares. Says the pitch has been a good one for the spinners as we have seen in the tournament so far. Observes that batting is relatively easy with the pace bowlers operating but that is where the overhead conditions come into play. Mentions that the batters will have to wait for the opportunities to score and once they are all set, the wicket becomes easy to bat on with the ball getting older.

The captain of India Women Under-19, Niki Prasad says they would have preferred to bat first and views this as a valuable opportunity for the team to put some runs on the board. She emphasizes that they will be challenged more in the next stage and says this game would be beneficial to help them build momentum. Prasad concludes by committing to giving their best performance and informs that they've made two changes.

The captain of Scotland Women Under-19, Niamh Muir says that they want to bowl first as there has been an overnight rain and it still looks a bit gloomy so they want to use the conditions to their advantage. She further adds that the tournament has been a good one for them and they are taking back a lot of learnings. She ends by saying that they are looking to give their all in their final game and will look to end the tournament on a high.

Scotland Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Pippa Kelly, Emma Walsingham, Pippa Sproul (WK), Niamh Muir (C), Nayma Sheikh, Charlotte Nevard (In for Rosie Speedy), Ammy Baldie, Gabriella Fontenla, Maisie Maceira, Mollie Parker (In for Molly Barbour-Smith), Kirsty McColl.

India Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Kamalini G (WK), Trisha Gongadi, Sanika Chalke, Niki Prasad (C), Ishwari Awasare, Mithila Vinod, Bhavika Ahire (In for Joshitha V J), Aayushi Shukla, Shabnam, Vaishnavi Sharma, Sonam Yadav (In for Parunika Sisodia).
TOSS UPDATE - Scotland Women Under-19 won the coin flip and they will BOWL first.

Will Scotland rise to the occasion and end their tournament on a high, or will India continue their dominant run and cruise to another easy win? All eyes will be on this exciting contest at Bayuemas Oval! Stay tuned for the Toss and other match updates!

Meanwhile, Scotland finds itself on the opposite end of the spectrum, having managed just one win in the tournament. With their semi-final hopes dashed, the Scottish team will look to end their campaign on a positive note. Players like Pippa Sproul and Maisie Maceira will need to step up if Scotland is to pose a challenge against a formidable Indian side.

Led by Niki Prasad, the Indian team has been a dominant force throughout the tournament, winning all four of their matches so far. They will look to continue their winning streak and maintain their momentum as they aim for a fifth consecutive victory. Key performers Gongadi Trisha and Vaishnavi Sharma have been standout players for India, excelling with the bat and ball, respectively, and are expected to play pivotal roles once again.

Hello! A warm welcome to everyone joining us here today! India is all set to face Scotland in their second Super Six encounter of the ICC Women’s U19 T20 World Cup 2025. The match will take place at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur, with India already riding high after an emphatic 8-wicket win over Bangladesh in their previous Super Six match. That victory also secured India’s place in the semi-finals, keeping their unbeaten streak alive in the tournament.
... MATCH DAY ...

The second edition of the ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup has seen new stars rise on the international arena and we have now reached the final round of fixtures of the Super Six stage of the competition. In March that of the Super Six stage it will be a Group 1 fixture where India Women Under-19 will take on Scotland Women Under-19 at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur. India, who are the inaugural and the reigning champions have hardly broken a sweat this far in the competition and have already sealed a semifinal spot whereas Scotland have bettered their performance from the previous World Cup by making past the initial group stage. In a tournament that has been married by rain and a lot of low scores, the bowlers have definitely enjoyed and India's Vaishnavi Sharma leads the charts with 9 wickets to her name, including a stellar five-wicket haul. India Women Under-19 will be expected to brush aside Scotland Women Under-19 and storm into the semifinals unbeaten but the minnows will certainly have a say as they are a disciplined outfit and won't bow down without a fight. Can Scotland Women Under-19 make history and script and unfathomable win? Or will India Women Under-19 continue to march on their merry way? Only time will tell.
